summary_html: The **Project Milk Carton AI Layer** performs cross-analysis of federal and state chains to identify weak points, policy gaps, and non-compliance. This is the citizen feedback mechanism for accountability and reform.
authority_html: No direct statutory authority — citizen innovation layer built on public data and federal transparency laws.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: News and Observer Publishing Co. v. Poole
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that SBI investigative reports submitted to a gubernatorial commission became the commission's public records, and that absent a clear statutory exemption all documents meeting the statutory definition of public records must be disclosed for public inspection.
key_cases.relevance: It supplies the legal baseline for citizen access to the state records on which independent analysis depends.
key_cases.quote: in the absence of clear statutory exemption or exception, documents falling within the definition of "public records" in the Public Records Law must be made available for public inspection

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the 'reasonable efforts' requirement of the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act creates no federal right enforceable by children or parents through § 1983 or an implied right of action; enforcement lies with the Secretary through the state-plan approval process.
key_cases.relevance: Any accountability layer built on federal child-welfare statutes must account for the absence of a private right of action.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.case_name: Virmani v. Presbyterian Health Services Corp.
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the public's qualified right of access to civil court proceedings and records under Article I, Section 18 was not violated by closing hearings and sealing materials, because the compelling statutory interest in confidential medical peer review outweighed that right and no lesser alternative would protect it.
key_cases.relevance: Any transparency demand must be measured against this compelling-interest and least-restrictive-alternative test.
key_cases.quote: the compelling countervailing public interest in such high quality public medical care overcomes the qualified public right to open civil court proceedings and records of those proceedings

key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that UNC-Chapel Hill must release as public records the name, violation and sanction of every student found responsible for violating its sexual assault policy, because FERPA permits but does not compel confidentiality and therefore does not preempt the mandate of North Carolina's Public Records Act.
key_cases.relevance: It is the current legal baseline for citizen demands for state records on which independent accountability analysis depends.
key_cases.quote: The Act is intended to be liberally construed to ensure that governmental records be open and made available to the public, subject only to a few limited exceptions.
